Hydration is the weight of water divided by the weight of flour in a bread dough. A seventy percent dough is easy to handle; eighty percent gives an open, glossy crumb but is sticky and slack. Whole wheat and rye absorb more water than white bread flour, so a recipe with whole grains needs higher hydration for the same feel. Autolyse, resting flour and water before adding the levain, makes wet doughs easier to work. Strong flour with more protein holds gas better during the rise and gives better [[Scoring and oven spring]].
